title: Ash Becomes Spring
source_seed: Seed 2/3 (Lalitopakhyana ch. 30): Shiva burned Kama to ashes and Lalita, moved by compassion, restores him. Invented symbol: the ash in her palm and the flower bud; the restoration is told in one devotional telling.
logline: Grey ash of the burned god of love gathers in her open palm, and her glance turns it into a blossom that blooms and sends a rush of petals into the sky.
story: Grey ash of the burned god of love gathers in her open palm, and her glance turns it into a blossom that blooms and sends a rush of petals into the sky. Seed 2/3 (Lalitopakhyana ch. 30): Shiva burned Kama to ashes and Lalita, moved by compassion, restores him. Invented symbol: the ash in her palm and the flower bud; the restoration is told in one devotional telling.
loop: The light settles and she rests in the frame-1 smile.
audio: Eerie and solemn: low drone, bowed tone, deep frame drums building faster at the payoff; tempo from the director (rule 8).

shots.camera: Eye level, front-facing, the tall crown and crescent moon centered and fully framed, full-length framing, slow push-in toward Her palms and face.
shots.action: Pale grey ash rises from the dark water in a thin stream and gathers in Her open right palm, a small grey mound resting on it, as Her compassionate gaze falls on it. Her hair settles under natural gravity.
shots.purpose: The ash is the burned Kama; her look is the turning point.

shots.camera: The slow push-in holds at eye level, the crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: The ash in Her palm glows rose-gold and swells into a blooming flower, and its petals lift off in a rising rush that spirals up past Her crown into the twilight sky as She smiles. Her hair settles under natural gravity.
shots.purpose: Compassion restores the god of love: ash becomes bloom.
